{"status":"done","summary":"Verified the card's root cause at source (service.ts) before fixing — confirmed as described: `recordDeployShasDelivered` was called unconditionally in `resumeFleetOnBoot`'s manager/platform branch, BEFORE the `isNoOpManagerWake` check, so it fired even when nothing was enqueued to the session (silent bystander) or when only a minimal draft/cap-note nudge with no SHA was sent. The old comment's premise ("an unaffected bystander still 'saw' it") was false — a silent resume enqueues literally nothing.

Commit bbe1970b. Regions touched in packages/daemon/src/sessions/service.ts: ~3950-3963 (docstring), ~4051-4057 (docstring), ~4117-4159 (the actual fix: moved the record call inside the `else` branch — the only one whose enqueued text names `intent.reason`/the SHA), ~7536-7731 (platformEscalate's suppression block + return type), ~8437-8452 (renamed `deployShaAlreadyDelivered`→`deployShasAlreadyDelivered`, now returns matched tokens instead of a boolean). All far from the other worker's 11180-11560 merge-admission region — no overlap.

DoD-1 (move the call): done, verified via a positive control — a silent bystander Lead that never saw a SHA no longer suppresses a later completion escalation naming it (new test 2a); a Lead that genuinely got the full re-orient nudge naming the SHA still correctly suppresses (test 2b).

DoD-2 (distinguishable suppressed result): added `"suppressed-duplicate"` to the shared `DeliveryStatus` union (packages/shared/src/types.ts) — set only when a LIVE Lead's nudge was deliberately skipped via SHA dedup, never conflated with `"boarded"` (genuinely no live Lead) again. Updated the `platform_escalate` tool description in mcp/orchestration.ts to document it.

DoD-3 (log the matched token): `deployShasAlreadyDelivered` now returns the actual matched tokens (not a boolean); the suppression log line names them, and they're also returned on the response as `suppressedShas` for programmatic recovery.

Fixed the stale comment that stated the false premise verbatim, in the same commit, per the card's instruction.

Did NOT touch the "6 suppressions" count, did not chase which token collided in old specimens, and left the wake-is-broken/card 4693a9b2 premise alone — all per the card's explicit prohibitions.

Verification: `pnpm build` clean (daemon+shared+web). Ran the directly affected test file `packages/daemon/test/restart-wake-classification.mjs` (which already covered this exact mechanism, card 5907b71e part 2) — I updated it since it had encoded the buggy behavior as expected (asserted a silent bystander's SHA-naming escalation was correctly suppressed, which was actually the bug). Rewrote part 2 into 2a (regression guard: silent bystander no longer wrongly suppresses) and 2b (positive control: a genuinely-notified Lead still correctly suppresses, with the new status + token). All 29 checks pass. Also ran 8 other tests touching `platformEscalate`/`DeliveryStatus` (worker-report-delivery-status, platform-messaging, platform-escalate-dedup, platform-escalate-parked-wake, platform-escalate-append, platform-cross-project-task, task-dedupe, arg-name-aliases) — all pass, no regressions since none combine resumeFleetOnBoot + the SHA-dedup path the way restart-wake-classification.mjs does.

Enumerated the directory-scanning test guards myself (`grep -l readdirSync packages/daemon/test/*guard*.mjs`, found 5, not trusting any prior count) and ran each bare (not piped): clock-path-regression-guard, codescape-privacy-guard, emit-compare-soundness-guard, fixed-wait-negative-guard, onexit-discard-guard — all exit 0.

Did not run the full gate (`run_gate`) — targeted tests + guards covered the change per the default; happy to run it if you want the shared-resource confirmation given the file-contention note.","managerTurnSeqAtReport":14}
